name: Kingdom of Kush (25th Dynasty, Shebitku)

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 600,000-700,000 km2 at 700 BCE for Egypt in the Kushite Period; Taagepera 1978 gives 0.5 million km2 for the 25th Dynasty at 715 BCE (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_empires). Border = historical-basemaps world_bc700 'Kush' (Nubia to ~16 N) + 'Egypt' (Nile valley and Delta), ~594,000 km2 computed from the GeoJSON.

population.note: Seshat codes 2,500,000-3,000,000 for Egypt in the Kushite Period (747-656 BCE); Nubia adds ~0.3-1.2 M (OWID/HYDE Sudan 1.2 M in 1000 BCE for all of modern Sudan, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true).

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Seshat codes the largest settlement at 65,000 (700 BCE; Memphis or Thebes); Nubia rural.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. No modern estimate of the Kushite army total exists. Context: the Kushite-Egyptian army fought Sennacherib at Eltekeh (701 BCE) and supported Judah; Assyrian records list horses and chariots of the king of Kush; Delta princes still kept their own Libyan warrior (machimoi) forces (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty-fifth_Dynasty_of_Egypt). Scaled from the Egyptian New Kingdom snapshots and the Assyrian opponent.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Delta machimoi and Kushite levies.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Chariot crews, Nile fleet crews, supply.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Kushite core warrior class plus Egyptian machimoi and levies.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. No modern estimate of the Kushite army total exists. Context: the Kushite-Egyptian army fought Sennacherib at Eltekeh (701 BCE) and supported Judah; Assyrian records list horses and chariots of the king of Kush; Delta princes still kept their own Libyan warrior (machimoi) forces (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty-fifth_Dynasty_of_Egypt). Scaled from the Egyptian New Kingdom snapshots and the Assyrian opponent. Split: Egyptian and Libyan spear infantry ~40% of personnel roles.

quality.note: Bronze and early iron weapons, shields; below Assyrian heavy infantry.

training.note: Machimoi warrior class and Kushite troops.

count.note: Educated guess. No modern estimate of the Kushite army total exists. Context: the Kushite-Egyptian army fought Sennacherib at Eltekeh (701 BCE) and supported Judah; Assyrian records list horses and chariots of the king of Kush; Delta princes still kept their own Libyan warrior (machimoi) forces (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty-fifth_Dynasty_of_Egypt). Scaled from the Egyptian New Kingdom snapshots and the Assyrian opponent. Split: Nubian archers ~43% (Ta-Seti, 'land of the bow'; long self bows and composite bows).

Educated guess. No modern estimate of the Kushite army total exists. Context: the Kushite-Egyptian army fought Sennacherib at Eltekeh (701 BCE) and supported Judah; Assyrian records list horses and chariots of the king of Kush; Delta princes still kept their own Libyan warrior (machimoi) forces (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty-fifth_Dynasty_of_Egypt). Scaled from the Egyptian New Kingdom snapshots and the Assyrian opponent. Split: skirmishers and desert auxiliaries ~13%.
Educated guess. Kushite kings bred fine horses (Piye's horse burials at El-Kurru; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty-fifth_Dynasty_of_Egypt); mounted troops were few compared with chariots.

Educated guess. Kushite chariotry with prized Nubian horses (studies of horse skeletons at El-Kurru cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty-fifth_Dynasty_of_Egypt); Assyrian texts list Kushite horses taken in 671. Crews in supportPersonnel.

quality.note: Two-horse chariots, a generation behind Assyrian heavy chariots.

count.note: Educated guess. Nile war boats used by Piye in his Delta campaign (c. 728) for sieges of riverside towns; no count survives.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5: competent (Piye's Delta campaign, Taharqa's 674 repulse of Esarhaddon), but beaten at Eltekeh and by Assyria 671-663.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: dual Kushite-Egyptian monarchy with semi-autonomous Delta princes.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: religiously legitimised restoration of Egypt.

weapons.note: Between 2 and 3: bronze with spreading iron; behind Assyria.

ships.note: Between 2 and 3: Nile war fleet; little sea power.

fortification.note: Between 2 and 3: walled Egyptian cities and Nubian fortresses.

logistics.note: Between 2 and 3: Nile transport over 2,000 km with cataract portages.

communications.note: Between 2 and 3: royal couriers along the Nile.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 via https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true: Egypt 1 CE = 1,116 (2011 int$); Nubia poorer, Third Intermediate Period Egypt fragmented.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Wartime against Assyria; temple building in Egypt and Nubia.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Egyptian craft centres; Nubian gold.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Nile flood agriculture in Egypt; Nubia narrower floodplain.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots; Bronze Age life expectancy was if anything lower, so this is not an underestimate.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Desert tracks and Delta embankment roads; the Nile was the main artery.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Memphis, Thebes, Napata, Tanis, Sais (river ports); Pelusium on the coast.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Nile cargo boats; little sea trade.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Nile river supply; Levant operations short.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Cattle (Nubian herds), donkeys, horses; ~0.06-0.14 per inhabitant.

chokepoints: Wadi routes across the Bayuda desert

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: Nile cataracts, deserts and Nubian homeland depth (Assyria never entered Nubia).

notes: Snapshot = c. 700 BCE, Shebitku (Shabataka) ruling Kush and Egypt as the 25th Dynasty, between Eltekeh (701) and Taharqa's accession (690). Region = subsaharan_africa per the coverage plan although most population lived in Egypt. Forces are educated guesses: no ancient or modern total exists. Population convention: Egypt and Nubia inside the border.
